label: TP
reason: Both alerts represent genuine vulnerabilities. Alert 1 (java/xss): User-controlled data from HTTP header flows through URL decode/Base64 roundtrip to 'bar', then to 'fileName' which is HTML-encoded before printing to response. Per balanced encoding rule, presence of encodeForHTML on attacker-controlled data prefers alert-TP. Alert 2 (java/path-injection): Same user-controlled data reaches 'fileName' (line 59) which is used in FileOutputStream constructor, enabling path manipulation within TESTFILES_DIR. Both sinks receive attacker-controlled input.

evidence.note: User input from request header flows through URL decode and Base64 roundtrip to bar, then combined with TESTFILES_DIR to form fileName which is HTML-encoded and printed to response writer (XSS sink)
Same user-controlled bar value reaches fileName (line 59) which is used in FileOutputStream constructor, representing path injection vulnerability
